acceptance_criteria.criterion: First scan of a folder containing supported-extension files produces one Inserted outcome per file.
Second scan produces SkippedAlreadyKnown for all previously-inserted files.
Files with unsupported extensions produce SkippedUnsupportedExtension without any catalog writes.
A per-file hasher exception produces Failed and does not abort the remaining scan.
A file whose absolute path exceeds 250 UTF-8 bytes produces RefreshOutcome.Failed with a Warning log entry and no DB write.
Cancellation via CancellationToken stops processing between files without throwing to the caller.
Progress events carry monotonically-increasing Processed counts.
No Task.Run or Thread usage exists in the implementation.

comments.note: LibraryScanner.RefreshAsync enumerates all files eagerly into a List before processing to compute an accurate Total. For extremely large libraries (millions of files) this could consume significant memory. A streaming approach with a two-pass or estimated Total would be more scalable, but the current approach matches the plan spec and is acceptable for M3.

ProcessFileAsync checks the extension using TryGetObfuscatedExtension (real→obfuscated lookup) and IsObfuscated (obfuscated→real lookup). This is correct but slightly non-obvious — a dedicated IObfuscationMap.IsSupportedExtension(ext) helper would be more expressive. Noted for a future interface revision.

The path-length constant MaxPathUtf8Bytes = 250 is defined in LibraryScanner with no accompanying explanation of its origin (legacy DB column width or OS constraint). A code comment or link to the spec would improve maintainability.

summary: Reviewed 3 files: LibraryScanner.cs, InMemoryMovieCatalogRepository.cs, LibraryScannerTests.cs. 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium, 2 Low (recorded). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: Low | A01 (Broken Access Control) — src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/Library/LibraryScanner.cs:88 | Directory.EnumerateFiles with SearchOption.AllDirectories follows symbolic links (Windows junction points, Unix symlinks). If an attacker with local filesystem write access can plant a symlink inside a registered library folder, the scanner will traverse into the symlink target. Risk is limited: (1) library folder paths originate from ILibraryFolderRepository — a trusted internal source, not user-supplied input; (2) the scanner only reads files to compute hashes, no write operations occur. Remediation (optional, defence-in-depth): skip symlinked entries using FileInfo.LinkTarget != null or FileAttributes.ReparsePoint before processing.

Low | A09 (Security Logging & Monitoring) — src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/Library/LibraryScanner.cs:149 | Absolute file paths logged at Warning level may include OS user-identifiable components (e.g. C:\Users\<username>\...). Structured logging with named placeholders is used correctly — no log injection risk. If log output is forwarded to an external SIEM or shared log store, consider scrubbing or truncating paths to remove personal directory segments. No immediate action required.

All OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed. No Critical or High issues identified. Code has no user-controlled path injection, no deserialization, no external process spawning, no cryptographic misuse, no hardcoded secrets, and no new third-party dependencies.

summary: Code review PASS. No blocking issues. Three Fix-Forward improvements applied directly to LibraryScanner.cs (non-behavioral): (1) added origin comment to MaxPathUtf8Bytes referencing the MariaDB varchar(255) column constraint, (2) added clarifying comment to the obfuscation-aware extension check explaining why two lookups are needed, (3) wrapped the outcomes dictionary in ReadOnlyDictionary<RefreshOutcome,int> in BuildSummary to be consistent with progress reporting and make the immutability intent explicit. Build and all 11 LibraryScanner tests pass after changes.

comments.note: Added origin comment to MaxPathUtf8Bytes = 250 in LibraryScanner.cs. The constant originates from the MariaDB movies_filenames.filename column (varchar(255), utf8mb4), as documented in plan.md line 753. A 5-byte margin is kept to avoid hitting the column limit on multi-byte trailing characters. Without this comment the magic number was opaque to future maintainers.

Added clarifying comment to the extension check in ProcessFileAsync (LibraryScanner.cs). The check uses TryGetObfuscatedExtension (native→obfuscated lookup, i.e., is it a real extension?) combined with IsObfuscated (obfuscated→native lookup, i.e., is it an obfuscated extension?). This is correct behaviour but non-obvious; the comment explains why both lookups are needed.

Wrapped the outcomes dictionary in new ReadOnlyDictionary<RefreshOutcome, int>(outcomes) inside BuildSummary. Previously the mutable local Dictionary was passed directly as IReadOnlyDictionary — technically safe since the method exits immediately after, but asymmetric with progress reporting (which always copies the dictionary). The ReadOnlyDictionary wrapper makes the immutability guarantee explicit and prevents accidental mutation via cast. No behaviour change; all 11 tests continue to pass.

[documentation-forward] The 250-byte path-length guard in LibraryScanner.cs now has a code comment, but the milestone doc (plan.md line 753) states 'Document the 255-byte path limit in the milestone doc as a known M3 constraint.' This obligation is still open — the Documentation agent should add a Known Constraints or Limitations section to the M3 milestone documentation covering: (a) the MariaDB varchar(255) column limit on movies_filenames.filename, (b) the 250 UTF-8-byte effective guard (5-byte margin for multi-byte trailing characters), and (c) the AC-5 test skip condition on Windows when %TEMP% paths are already long.

The eager file enumeration in RefreshAsync (collecting all files into a List<> before processing) is a known trade-off documented by the Developer. For M3 library sizes this is acceptable. If library growth becomes a concern, a future revision could stream files per-folder with an estimated Total, or use two-pass enumeration.
